what_its_for: Ursodiol is used to dissolve small gallstones in people who cannot have surgery, to prevent gallstones from forming in people losing weight quickly, and to treat a liver disease called primary biliary cholangitis (PBC). It works by reducing the amount of cholesterol made by your liver and slowly breaking down cholesterol-based gallstones.
how_to_take: Take ursodiol exactly as your doctor prescribed. Swallow the capsules or tablets whole with a full glass of water. Take it with food or milk to help prevent an upset stomach. Try to take it at the same time(s) every day to keep a steady level of the medicine in your body. Do not crush, chew, or break the tablets unless your doctor tells you it is okay.
dosing: Your dose depends on your weight and what condition is being treated. For gallstone dissolving, the usual dose is 8 to 10 mg per kilogram of body weight per day, divided into 2 or 3 doses taken with meals. For preventing gallstones during rapid weight loss, the typical dose is 300 mg twice a day. For primary biliary cholangitis, the dose is usually 13 to 15 mg per kilogram per day in 2 to 4 divided doses. Always follow the exact dose your doctor prescribes.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store ursodiol at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. Do not use after the expiration date printed on the label. Ask your pharmacist how to safely dispose of any unused medication.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking antacids that contain aluminum (such as Maalox or Mylanta) at the same time as ursodiol, as they can prevent your body from absorbing it properly. If you need an antacid, take it at least 2 hours before or after your ursodiol dose. Avoid cholesterol-lowering medicines called bile acid sequestrants (such as cholestyramine or colestipol) at the same time for the same reason. Talk to your doctor before starting any new medicines, vitamins, or supplements. Try to avoid high-fat, high-cholesterol foods, as these can make gallstones worse.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience severe stomach pain, nausea, or vomiting that does not go away; yellowing of your skin or the whites of your eyes (jaundice); dark urine or very pale stools; unusual tiredness or weakness; signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, itching, swelling of the face, lips, or throat, or difficulty breathing. Also call your doctor if your symptoms do not improve or if they get worse.
when_it_works: Ursodiol works slowly. It may take several months before you notice improvement. For dissolving gallstones, it can take 6 to 24 months of treatment, and not all gallstones will dissolve completely. For liver disease (PBC), it may take weeks to months to see improvements in your lab results. Do not stop taking it on your own even if you feel fine — continue taking it as long as your doctor tells you to.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Ursodiol is sometimes used during pregnancy for certain liver conditions, but only under close medical supervision. Breastfeeding: It is not fully known if ursodiol passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. Elderly patients: No special dose adjustments are typically needed, but your doctor may monitor you more closely. Children: This medicine may be used in children for certain liver conditions, but dosing will be carefully determined by the child's doctor based on weight.
